issues.title: All-wave smoke enumerates 36 waves while active authority is closed at 35
issues.defect: Current main smoke includes 36 waves including Asian Barometer W6, while the governed runtime wave registry is explicitly CLOSED_35_WAVES and current question-relation authority excludes Asian W6 from active governed scope.
issues.evidence: Main/runtime reconciliation and authority-scope count: governed Asian waves are W1/W4/W5; W6 is excluded.
issues.consequence: The acceptance harness asks the pipeline to execute a wave its authority layer says must not enter the active universe.
issues.required: Use the governed 35-wave registry as the smoke scope source instead of a divergent hard-coded list. Asian W6 must remain excluded unless authority is explicitly reopened.
tests: Smoke scope exactly equals governed active-wave registry.
Asian Barometer W6 is absent under current authority.

issues.title: Default all-wave smoke requires joint-family authority the project does not possess
issues.defect: The default all-wave harness requires every governed wave to have executable V550J family authority. The default family registry does not cover the all-wave universe; executable coverage was 8/35 in the permissive runtime interpretation and 0/36 in current main because main correctly rejects draft registry status.
issues.evidence: Executed/derived joint-authority coverage during exhaustive audit.
issues.consequence: The default acceptance harness is structurally incapable of passing before reaching most pipeline semantics; absence of optional/applicability-scoped joint authority is mislabeled as pipeline failure.
issues.required: Separate base V550→V552J universality from V550J/V551J applicability. Joint stages should run where governed family authority exists and report typed not-applicable/coverage debt elsewhere; do not require nonexistent authority globally.
tests: Default all-wave smoke can run the governed 35-wave base universe without requiring nonexistent joint-family definitions.
Joint authority coverage is reported explicitly and only gates applicable scopes.

issues.title: Compilers advertise CSV-only/no-Parquet modes that the pipeline cannot honor
issues.affected: V550J/V551/V551J/V552/V552J CLI write-format flags and downstream consumers
issues.defect: Relevant compilers expose `--no-write-parquet`, but lineage/smoke/consumers hard-code Parquet paths. V552 even unconditionally writes `manifest/v552_input_atoms.parquet` before its governed output loop, so the advertised switch is not internally truthful. V552J can read CSV fallback and then separately block because the Parquet path is absent.
issues.evidence: Format-contract trace across producer CLIs and immediate consumers.
issues.consequence: Operator-visible configuration can create unsupported or internally contradictory runs; output-format choice becomes accidental semantic availability.
issues.required: Choose one real contract: either Parquet is mandatory for governed pipeline runs and fake flexibility is removed, or consumers resolve artifacts from producer manifests and support each advertised format consistently.
tests: Every advertised write-format mode is consumable end-to-end, or unsupported modes are removed/rejected.

issues.title: Reusing a run directory can make consumers ingest stale artifacts from a previous execution
issues.affected: Stage writers using existing run directories + consumers preferring/hard-coding prior-format files
issues.defect: Run directories are reused non-transactionally and disabling an output format does not remove an older copy. A rerun under the same run ID can therefore leave stale Parquet beside newly written CSV; downstream consumers that prefer/hard-code Parquet can ingest the previous execution's bytes.
issues.evidence: Static writer/reader path trace. A runtime Parquet microtest could not execute in the audit environment because pyarrow was unavailable; the filesystem selection path itself is deterministic.
issues.consequence: Fresh outputs can be silently contaminated by stale artifacts while directory/run names still look correct.
issues.required: Use fresh/transactional run directories or atomically clear/replace stage-owned artifacts before publication. Consumers must bind to producer-manifest-declared artifact hashes rather than discover files by preferred extension.
tests: Rerunning same run ID cannot leave a disabled-format artifact visible as current.
Consumer reads only producer-declared current artifact hashes.
issues.note: Static defect confirmed; pyarrow absence prevented one optional execution reproduction.

issues.title: Section85 source transfer did not rebase old package paths
issues.defect: The curated transfer moved the package under `section85/`, but runners, tests, execution instructions, and authority metadata still reference the former `85_V550J_BOUNDED_NINE_FAMILY_AUTHORITY_ADAPTER_AND_CANARY/...` root; the diagnostic smoke runner also hard-codes Desktop absolute authority paths.
issues.evidence: With repo PYTHONPATH, 15/16 Section85 tests failed on nonexistent old paths. Temporary path alias made 14/16 pass; the remaining two depend on excluded generated outputs.
issues.consequence: Regression safeguards for main-only V550J authority features are effectively broken, and bounded diagnostic execution depends on obsolete filesystem layout/Desktop state.
issues.required: Rebase all Section85 internal paths to repository-relative `section85/` locations; remove Desktop absolute paths; convert the two generated-output-dependent tests to fixtures or explicit integration tests.
tests: Section85 tests run from clean checkout without path alias or Desktop files.
No active Section85 code/authority metadata references the obsolete package prefix.

issues.title: Section85 bounded gate treats presence of any V552J readiness document as success
issues.defect: The gate computes `v552j_readiness_present = bool(v552j_ready)`, so a nonempty readiness object that explicitly says BLOCKED still satisfies the presence check.
issues.consequence: A blocked V552J run can satisfy a bounded functional acceptance condition solely because its failure report exists.
issues.required: Parse and require the typed compatible V552J run-integrity/evidence/permission state. File/object presence is not readiness.
tests: BLOCKED V552J readiness never passes the gate.
Valid no-evidence state can pass integrity while remaining correctly non-sufficient for evidence-dependent operations.
